import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 194

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

## Counterexample

The conjecture is false. Take a clique on vertices `0, ..., 10`, four additional vertices
`11, ..., 14` adjacent to every clique vertex, and three leaves attached at `11`, `12`, and `14`.
This connected graph has independence number `4`, while the sum of the independence numbers of its
vertex neighbourhoods is `54`, so their average is `3`. Thus it satisfies the conjecture's
hypothesis with equality. However, its three leaves would all have to be endpoints of a Hamiltonian
path, which is impossible.
-/

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture194

open SimpleGraph

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 194](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, if `α(G) ≤ 1 + l_avg(G)`, then `G` has a Hamiltonian path.
Here `α(G) = G.indepNum` is the independence number, and
`l_avg(G) = averageIndepNeighbors G` is the average over all vertices of the independence number
of the neighbourhood.
A Hamiltonian path is a walk visiting every vertex exactly once. The answer is no, as witnessed by
the 18-vertex graph described above.

Counterexample (Graph6): `Q~~~~~~~~~~~~}~}^~??G??_??_`

-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/anagnorisis2peripeteia/formal-conjectures/blob/4bff865a14c2cd61fefbffbe9c49cbfc5a89ac45/FormalConjectures/WrittenOnTheWallII/GraphConjecture194.lean#L128-L140"]
theorem conjecture194 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) (_h : G.Connected),
      (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ 1 + averageIndepNeighbors G →
      ∃ a b : α, ∃ p : G.Walk a b, p.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The average indep-neighbors invariant `l G` is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ averageIndepNeighbors G := by
  apply div_nonneg
  · apply Finset.sum_nonneg
    intro v _
    exact Nat.cast_nonneg _
  · exact Nat.cast_nonneg _

/-- The edgeless graph on 2 vertices has 2 vertices. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : Fintype.card (Fin 2) = 2 := by decide

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture194

reformulations.difference: The source explicitly requires a path. Lean quantifies a walk and requires `p.IsHamiltonian`, without separately asserting `p.IsPath`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `Walk.IsHamiltonian` requires every vertex to occur exactly once in the support. This implies duplicate-free support and hence `p.IsPath`. Conversely, a path containing every vertex has each support count equal to one. The equivalence `p.IsHamiltonian ↔ p.IsPath ∧ ∀ v, v ∈ p.support` was proved in /workspace/review/boundaries.lean.

review.notes: The theorem and both sanity checks are faithful. The source explicitly assumes n > 1, matching `Nontrivial`; the independence numbers, neighborhood average, inequality, and quantifier scopes agree. Lean boundary tests cover empty, singleton, and smallest permitted vertex types. Independent computation confirms that the Graph6 string exactly matches the described graph, with independence number 4 and neighborhood sum 54, hence average 3; its three leaves prevent a Hamiltonian path. Lean computes the same invariants. The cited external proof compiled in /workspace/review/CitedProofCheck.lean after import/namespace-only changes, and its theorem type was checked definitionally equal to the reviewed declaration. Its axioms include native_decide-generated evaluation axioms, but no sorryAx. The latest accessible source snapshot (26 July 2026) still labels 194 'O', meaning 'open (as far as I know)'; the live site was unavailable. This is catalogue lag, not an incorrect repository status: the negative answer and solved tag are supported by the verified counterexample and cited proof.
